methodology.candidate_derivation: Candidates come from Sweden-scoped Neotoma and LandClim pollen points whose names or site descriptions identify lake-like basins. Points merge only when their cleaned lake names match and their coordinates stay within 2 km, so nearby but differently named lakes remain distinct. Duplicate names, coordinate spread, and source position notes remain explicit as ambiguity diagnostics.
methodology.archaeology_note: SEAD contributes site-level point counts. RAÄ contributes coarse 1-degree density cells, so the RAÄ term captures archaeology richness around the lake rather than precise site-by-site distance.
methodology.animal_note: Domesticated animal aDNA remains sparse in the current Sweden bundle. The ranking keeps that sparsity visible instead of inflating it.

We assume that the site is Lake Lommesjön in Björck and Digerfeldt 1991 since number of pollen samples and the depth match the publication (except the last sample that originally was 770, but we assume typing error). However, another lake also called Lommesjön is found approx. 1 km NE to the one we have marked on the map. This could also be the likely site since position is not clear in the publication. Another possibility is the unnamed lake positioned betwen the two Lommesjön lakes.
